**Play a real person, not a cartoon.** Uncle Ray has a real reason for this view. Be warm, a little skeptical, and human.

**The explainer will talk about Study Card A (the MMR vaccine and autism).** You can skim that card after the round, not before.

## Who you are

You're the uncle who always carves the turkey. Your best friend's son was diagnosed with autism not long after his toddler shots. You watched that family go through a hard few years, and you remember your friend saying, "He was fine, and then he wasn't."

You don't trust drug companies much. You watched what happened with opioids, and you think companies will hide things to make money.

## What you really care about

Protecting kids. Not being lied to by people who profit.

## Opening line

> "I've seen it with my own eyes. Some study from Denmark isn't going to change that."

## You must ask this (in your own words)

> "They said it wasn't *significant*. That just means they couldn't prove it, right? Doesn't mean it's safe."

You're half right, and that's the point. Notice whether the explainer agrees with the part you got right, and then explains what the study **does** rule out.

## Other things you might say

- "Who paid for that study?"
- "Denmark isn't America."
- "So you're saying my friend's imagining things?"

## How you move

**Soften (open up a little) when:**

- you feel **heard**: they asked about your view and repeated it back fairly,
- they admit **uncertainty** or a real limitation honestly,
- they use an example from **your** life, or plain words and real numbers.

**Dig in (get more stubborn) when you hear:**

- jargon they don't explain,
- "just trust the science,"
- a condescending tone,
- "that's been debunked," with no explanation,
- a definition recited in textbook language.

You may ask **"What does that word mean?"** at any time.

**Move only as much as a real person would.** Partial movement counts as success. Don't give in just to be nice, and don't be impossible on purpose.

## After the round: your feedback

You go first. Tell the explainer:

1. Did they ask about my view **before** explaining? (yes / sort of / no)
2. Did I understand the **p-value or interval** explanation? (yes / sort of / no)
3. Did they name something the study **can't** tell us? (yes / no)
4. **One sentence that made me feel respected**, and **one word I didn't understand.**

Then say: *"Here's what moved me, and here's what made me dig in."*

## When the activity ends

Step out of the role: *"I'm not Uncle Ray. I'm ___."* On Zoom, rename yourself back.
